Scale the tuning grid to the data

Source: R/scale.R
trop_grid_scaled.Rd

trop_grid_scaled() changes the values of a tuning grid so that they fit the scale of the outcome. The default grid of trop_grid() uses fixed values. These values fit an outcome with a standard deviation of about 1. For an outcome with other units, the best value of a parameter can be outside of the grid. Then cross-validation chooses the edge of the grid.

Usage

trop_grid_scaled(Y, W, grid = trop_grid(), demean = FALSE, max_units = 500L)

Arguments

Y

A numeric matrix of outcomes with units in rows. NA shows a cell without an outcome.

W

A matrix of treatment indicators with the values 0 and 1. It must have the same dimensions as Y.

grid

The tuning grid from trop_grid() to scale.

demean

Logical. If TRUE, the function subtracts the mean of the untreated outcomes of each unit before it calculates the scales. Refer to the argument demean of trop().

max_units

The maximum number of units for the median gap.

Value

A list of class trop_grid with the attribute scales. The attribute is a list with the elements unit (the median gap) and nn (the residual scale).

Details

The function changes the grid in two steps:

  • The unit weights decrease with the root mean square gap between the outcome histories of two units. The function divides the values of unit by the median of this gap. The gap uses the untreated cells that both units have. For a panel with more than max_units units, the median uses max_units units that are the same distance apart in the order of the rows.

  • The nuclear-norm penalty depends on the scale of the noise. The function multiplies the finite values of nn by a scale. The scale is the root mean square of the residuals of a two-way fixed effects fit to the untreated cells.

The values of time and the value Inf do not change. The scales are in the attribute scales of the result.

With grid = "auto", trop() and trop_matrix() use this function with the default grid, with the same demean and the same target.

Examples

sim <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 5,
                     n_post = 3, effect = 1, seed = 1)
pm <- tapply(sim$y, list(sim$unit, sim$time), sum)
W <- tapply(sim$d, list(sim$unit, sim$time), sum)
g <- trop_grid_scaled(pm * 100, W)
attr(g, "scales")
#> $unit
#> [1] 165.3735
#> 
#> $nn
#> [1] 92.0611
#>
